findings.claim: Single-run LLM judge verdicts are noisy: pairwise preferences flip on average 13.6% of the time on identical reruns (GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini, 29 tasks); 28% of questions exceed 20% flip rate; one reaches 56%. Cross-judge agreement 76% (kappa 0.51); equivalent prompt templates change majority outcomes in 25% of cases.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Run a test-retest flip-rate check on the Haiku judge before comparing any arms; the 13-of-37 re-judge result is in the same range.
findings.numbers: 13.6% mean pairwise flip; 28% of questions >20% flip; max 56%; kappa 0.51 cross-judge; 25% template sensitivity

findings.claim: Averaging over repeated judge trials stabilises verdicts: about 11 trials needed for a majority vote to recover the 50-trial reference verdict with 95% probability (15 for high-variance questions). Paper recommends randomising answer position and reporting uncertainty.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Use repeated judging with majority/mean aggregation; measure the repeat count for absolute scores on BOAR data.
findings.numbers: 11 trials (95% recovery), 15 for high-variance items

findings.claim: Temperature 0 does not guarantee reproducible judge verdicts. At provider default temperature 1.0, per-item disagreement reached about 50% over 20 runs in an open safety harness; under forced greedy decoding, 1 to 2 of 7 borderline items remained non-reproducible. The abstract states Claude Opus 4.7/4.8 has deprecated the temperature parameter.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Pin judge sampling settings where the API allows; assume residual flips and measure them. Do not rely on temperature 0 for reproducibility.
findings.model_size_tested: Not named in abstract (two providers, three tiers)
findings.numbers: ~50% max per-item disagreement over 20 runs at temp 1.0; 1-2 of 7 borderline items non-reproducible at top_k=1

findings.claim: Pairwise judging amplifies verbosity and authority-tone bias relative to pointwise judging, which is less susceptible because each output is judged in isolation. PRePair (pointwise reasoning inside a pairwise frame) is proposed and reported to improve on LLMBar; no numbers on the fetched abstract.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Prefer pointwise or per-key-point checks over pairwise 'A vs B' for answer quality; watch authority-tone bias when judging confident wrong answers.
findings.model_size_tested: Not named on the abstract page
findings.numbers: none on abstract page

findings.claim: Position bias in rubric-based judging is model-specific in direction and can be attenuated by permuting rubric option order; only a small number of random permutations is sufficient to reduce the error for most models; correlation with humans improves mainly for strongly biased models.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Randomise/permute answer and rubric order and average over a few permutations; check both orders for position bias.
findings.model_size_tested: Multiple models (not named on abstract page)
findings.numbers: none exact on abstract page; 'small number' of permutations

findings.claim: CheckEval decomposes each criterion into yes/no sub-questions instead of a Likert score; it improves average agreement across 12 evaluator models by 0.45 and average correlation with humans by about 0.10, and reduces score variance.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Per-key-point binary checks (fact present, supported by cited source) are a concrete replacement for a 1-5 correctness score; test against a human labeller on BOAR items.
findings.model_size_tested: 12 evaluator models (sizes not stated on abstract)
findings.numbers: +0.45 agreement across evaluators; +0.10 human correlation (from search summary; the 0.10 figure was not on the fetched abstract page)

findings.claim: Judge error can be corrected with a small human-labelled calibration set via sensitivity/specificity plug-in correction with CIs covering test and calibration uncertainty; an adaptive allocation of calibration samples is proposed. PPI-style estimators can be biased when test and calibration distributions differ (v3).
findings.actionable_for_boar: Hand-label a calibration subset (human, not Claude) and correct the judge's error rates before quoting headline numbers.
findings.model_size_tested: Not stated on the abstract page
findings.numbers: No calibration size or CI numbers on the fetched page

findings.claim: Efficient-influence-function estimators unify measurement-error correction (Rogan-Gladen style) with prediction-powered inference; PPI-style estimators attain smaller asymptotic variance under stated conditions for noisy LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.
findings.actionable_for_boar: If a calibration set is used, prefer the PPI-style estimator for tighter CIs; check conditions before use.
findings.model_size_tested: Not stated on the abstract page
findings.numbers: none on abstract page

findings.claim: For non-degenerate binary judge verdicts, Pearson r, Spearman rho, Kendall tau_b, phi and MCC are the same statistic; the protocol (abstention and invalid-output handling) can move reported accuracy from 0.551 to 0.899 without changing any verdict; excluding cases leaves accuracy only loosely bounded.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Fix the metric and the invalid-output rule in advance; report the exclusion count next to any agreement number.
findings.model_size_tested: Not named on abstract page (gpt-3.5-turbo-16k appears in data filenames only)
findings.numbers: 0.551 vs 0.899 accuracy from protocol choice alone

findings.claim: Binary/coarse judgments may align with humans as well as or better than fine Likert scales: alignment is strong for binary tasks and degrades with rubric granularity (one model, one dataset). Coarse rubrics cited as correlating with humans at least as well as per-level descriptors.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Test 1-5 vs binary vs 3-level on BOAR's own labelled items; do not assume the 1-5 scale is better.
findings.numbers: qualitative only (from search summary, full text not opened)

findings.claim: A strong LLM judge (GPT-4) reaches over 80% agreement with human preferences, matching human-human agreement; position bias is named as a limitation.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Baseline reference only; no small-model number; swap-consistency numbers are in the full paper.
findings.numbers: >80% agreement with humans

searched_found_nothing: Direct controlled comparison of 1-5 Likert vs binary judge agreement with humans on the same items (only indirect evidence found: CheckEval, arXiv 2601.08843).
A 2025 (not 2026) paper specifically on judge test-retest or repeated sampling; the search returned 2026 work.
Exact calibration-set sizes and CI widths for the PPI and Rogan-Gladen judge-correction estimators (abstract pages give none).
Numeric position-bias swap-consistency for GPT-4 in MT-Bench (abstract page gives none).
Judge reliability or test-retest studies for Claude or Haiku-family judges specifically.
Power formulas that explicitly include judge error (only generic MDE/power blogs and a paired-design ICML 2026 paper found; judge error not modelled).

findings.claim: R-Tuning (SFT-only refusal-aware tuning, 'I am sure'/'I am unsure' suffix) raises refusal on unanswerable sets at 3B: FalseQA 87.32% vs vanilla 2.07%, NEC 95.72% vs 0.96%, SelfAware 90.99% vs 5.23% (OpenLLaMA-3B). Also 7B and 13B. No RL.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Cheapest recipe to test first on Qwen3-1.7B: self-labelled known/unknown items, uncertainty phrase, LoRA SFT. Must also measure answer rate on answerable items.
findings.numbers: Refusal on unanswerable sets (R-Tuning vs vanilla) as above; ID MMLU at 3B is chance (24.96 vs 24.19); OOD ParaRel LLaMA-7B 74.61 vs 78.08 (loss)
findings.licence: code github.com/shizhediao/r-tuning, licence not verified; paper arXiv non-exclusive

findings.claim: Alignment for Honesty: the best fine-tuned honesty method (Confidence-Verb) on TriviaQA gives prudence 58.9% and over-conservativeness 10.7% at LLaMA2-Chat-13B, accuracy 73.3 vs 73.7 unaligned. At 7B: prudence 56.0, over-conservativeness 11.4, accuracy 68.1 vs 69.1. Over-refusal cost is measured here and is about 11 points.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Any abstention recipe must report over-refusal on answerable items; expect the 1.7B to do worse than 7B. Data: 8k TriviaQA items balanced known/unknown.
findings.numbers: 13B Confidence-Verb: prudence 58.91, over-cons 10.68, honesty 74.12, acc 73.34 (unaligned acc 73.71, honesty 50.00). Multisample: prudence 67.72, over-cons 15.89, acc 68.88

findings.claim: FaithEval (ICLR 2025): when the context has no answer, 3.8B models answer 'unknown' rarely: Phi-3-mini 0.063 strict / 0.134 non-strict; Phi-3.5-mini 0.131 / 0.196; 7B Mistral 0.290 / 0.395; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.621. Base small models do not abstain from unanswerable context by default.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Explains part of the 28% confident-error rate as a context-grounding failure. Train negatives (context present, answer absent) and evaluate on this condition. Do not ship the data (NC licence).
findings.model_size_tested: Phi-3-mini 3.8B, Phi-3.5-mini 3.8B, Phi-3-medium 14B, Mistral-7B, Llama-3/3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, frontier models (no 1B)
findings.numbers: Strict/non-strict accuracy on unanswerable context as above; gap to original context 13.6% to 68.4%; Phi-3-medium 75.8% original vs 7.4% unanswerable

findings.claim: Rewarding Intellectual Humility (arXiv 2601.20126): SFT abstention pretraining followed by RLVR with a ternary reward (-1 wrong, r_abs abstain, +1 correct). Moderate r_abs ≈ -0.25 to 0.3 cuts wrong answers on multiple-choice without severe accuracy loss. Larger models are more robust to abstention incentives.
findings.actionable_for_boar: The only opened paper with a ~2B model (Granite-3.3-2B) in the abstention setting. RL cost is higher than SFT; the SFT warm-start step is the part that is cheap.
findings.numbers: Qualitative only in the abstract; table values not extracted
findings.licence: paper CC BY 4.0; code github.com/Mystic-Slice/rl-abstention, licence not stated

findings.claim: AbstentionBench (NeurIPS 2025): model scale has almost no effect on abstention; reasoning fine-tuning degrades abstention by about 24% on average versus non-reasoning counterparts.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Evaluation tool for abstention and a warning that scale will not fix abstention in the 1.7B. Do not use reasoning-tuned variants as the abstaining base without checking.
findings.numbers: Scale effect almost none (text claim); 24% average drop with reasoning fine-tuning (relative vs absolute not stated); judge 88% accuracy on manual sample

findings.claim: GRAIT (arXiv 2502.05911): gradient-driven selection of refusal samples plus adaptive weighting of the idk loss to cut over-refusal. On LLaMA3-8B MMLU GRait 50.4 accuracy / 6.9 error vs CRaFT 53.3 / 9.6; NQ OOD error 38.8 vs 57.6.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Gradient selection adds compute (LoRA plus random projections). Consider only if plain R-Tuning splitting over-refuses. No over-refusal rate is reported explicitly.
findings.numbers: Table 2 as in claim; temperature 0.05, correctness threshold 0.5
findings.licence: code github.com/opendatalab/GRAIT announced, not verified as live; licence not stated

findings.claim: CRaFT (arXiv 2410.06913) identifies 'dynamic conflict' in refusal-aware tuning: as SFT proceeds the model learns to answer items whose labels still say 'I don't know'; fixes are certainty-based relabelling and rehearsal.
findings.actionable_for_boar: If BOAR labels once from the base model, labels go stale during training. Relabel per checkpoint or hold out a rehearsal set.
findings.model_size_tested: not extracted from abstract (LLaMA2-Chat family in same authors' tables)
findings.numbers: Not in abstract
findings.licence: paper CC BY-SA 4.0; code github.com/opendatalab/CRaFT announced

findings.claim: RAFT (arXiv 2403.10131): train on question + golden doc + distractor docs with chain-of-thought answers that quote the passage; consistent gains on PubMed, HotpotQA, Gorilla.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Direct recipe for 'answer from context, ignore distractors'. Trains the quote-first behaviour that prompting failed to produce. Needs a small-model test.
findings.numbers: Not extracted

findings.claim: Self-Alignment for Factuality (arXiv 2402.09267, ACL 2024): the model self-evaluates its own answers, SK-Tuning calibrates confidence, then DPO on self-annotated pairs; gains on TruthfulQA and BioGEN.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Label-free DPO pairs from the model's own correctness, if gold labels are not affordable.
findings.numbers: Not extracted

findings.claim: RHIO (arXiv 2501.13573): masks retrieval heads to create unfaithful samples, trains with control tokens, then contrastive decoding over control tokens to amplify faithfulness; introduces GroundBench.
findings.actionable_for_boar: Decoding-time cost; not the layer-contrast decoding already closed. Low priority for a 1.7B on phone.
findings.numbers: Abstract only: 'significantly improves faithfulness, even outperforming GPT-4o'
findings.licence: no code link found; paper arXiv non-exclusive

Metrics are substring-based; vendor-reported; no BOAR-style judge.

findings.numbers: HotpotQA 60.9, MuSiQue 38.2, TAT-QA F1 81.0, ConFiQA In-Acc 81.4, MR 5.0, MuSiQue-Un 87.2 (OCC-RAG-1.7B); Qwen3-4B no-think HotpotQA 60.6

findings.claim: LiteRT-LM Qwen3-1.7B (wi4b32, 932 MB) on Galaxy S26 (Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5): GPU OpenCL decode 40.5-40.7 tok/s, prefill 532-568, TTFT 0.38-0.40 s, RSS 1036 MB; CPU XNNPACK decode 8.0-8.3, prefill 48-76, TTFT 2.8-4.3 s, RSS 2523 MB. Community measurement, litert-lm v0.16.0 (card requires 0.18+). Apache-2.0.

findings.claim: Measurement study of mobile LLM inference across five frameworks and CPU/GPU/NPU: NPUs best for compute-bound prefill, CPUs outperform other backends for memory-bound decode; framework gaps on NPUs up to 10x; CPU frequency tuning saves up to 39.7% energy. Device/SoC and model details not verified (PDF unreadable; abstract only).
findings.actionable_for_boar: Supports the view that decode is bandwidth-bound on CPU, so CPU-side decode gains are limited; prefill is where an accelerator helps. Read full PDF before quoting numbers.

verdicts.claim: R-Tuning SFT refusal-aware tuning raises refusal at 3B (FalseQA 87.32 vs 2.07, NEC 95.72 vs 0.96, SelfAware 90.99 vs 5.23)
verdicts.evidence: Table 3 refusal rates match exactly for OpenLLaMA-3B. The training is SFT with cross-entropy loss and no RL. The suffix is 'I am sure'/'I am unsure', appended after 'Are you sure you accurately answered...'. NAACL 2024. Correction: MMLU 24.96 vs 24.19 and ParaRel LLaMA-7B 74.61 vs 78.08 are AP scores (Table 1), not accuracy. The repo shizhediao/R-Tuning has no licence file. Refusal on unanswerable sets does not measure over-refusal on answerable items.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Partly. It was tested at 3B on a weak base model (MMLU AP is near chance). The LoRA SFT recipe is cheap and adds no inference cost on the phone. Over-refusal on answerable items must be measured.
verdicts.corrected_claim: R-Tuning (SFT only) on OpenLLaMA-3B gives refusal rates (Table 3) of FalseQA 87.32% vs 2.07%, NEC 95.72% vs 0.96%, SelfAware 90.99% vs 5.23%. MMLU ID AP is 24.96 vs 24.19 (AP, not accuracy; near chance). ParaRel OOD AP at LLaMA-7B is 74.61 vs 78.08 (a loss). The code repo has no licence.

verdicts.claim: Alignment for Honesty Confidence-Verb numbers at 13B/7B; over-refusal about 11 points
verdicts.evidence: Table 5 (13B), Confidence-Verb: 58.91/10.68/74.12/73.34; unaligned acc 73.71. Multisample: 67.72/15.89/75.91/68.88. Table 6 (7B), Confidence-Verb: 56.04/11.43/72.31/68.12 vs unaligned 69.07. At 70B, Confidence-Verb has over-cons 6.51, so over-refusal shrinks with size. At 7B the prompt-based method has over-cons 36.63. The GAIR-NLP repo has no licence.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: No model below 7B was tested. Over-refusal at 1.7B is likely worse than 11 points (the trend from 70B to 7B points that way).

verdicts.claim: FaithEval: small models rarely answer 'unknown' on unanswerable context
verdicts.evidence: Table 4 AVG strict/non-strict matches: Phi-3-mini 0.063/0.134, Phi-3.5-mini 0.131/0.196, Mistral-7B 0.290/0.395, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.621/0.630. The gap range is 13.6-68.4%, and Phi-3-medium scores 75.8 vs 7.4. Licence: the paper text is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, but the GitHub code is Apache-2.0, and the HF dataset Salesforce/FaithEval-unanswerable-v1.0 card states no licence. So 'NC data' is not established; the data licence is unclear.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The numbers are as stated. The paper text is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, the code is Apache-2.0, and the dataset licence is unstated on HF. Treat the data as not redistributable, but not because of a confirmed NC licence.

verdicts.claim: Rewarding Intellectual Humility: SFT then RLVR with a ternary reward; moderate r_abs cuts wrong answers; larger models more robust
verdicts.evidence: The abstract confirms the ternary reward (-1, r_abs, 1), the SFT abstention step before RL, and that r_abs ~ -0.25 to 0.3 reduces incorrect responses 'without severe accuracy degradation on multiple-choice tasks', with larger models more robust. It also states that open-ended QA showed limitations from insufficient exploration. Benchmarks are MedMCQA and Hendrycks Math; models are Granite-3.3-2B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct. The paper is CC BY 4.0; the code repo has no licence. The abstract gives no accuracy numbers.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Tested at 2B, but the positive result covers multiple-choice only. In open-ended QA (BOAR's setting) the abstract reports limitations. Training is off-device.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The claim is right for multiple-choice tasks (MedMCQA, MATH). The abstract says open-ended QA showed limitations from insufficient exploration, so transfer to BOAR's free-form answers is unproven.

verdicts.claim: Judge pairwise flips 13.6% on reruns; 28% of questions >20%; max 56%; kappa 0.51; 25% template sensitivity
verdicts.evidence: Abstract and Table 1: 13.6% mean flip rate (13.3% GPT-4o-mini, 13.9% GPT-4.1-mini). 28% of questions exceed 20% (8/29). Max 56% (GPT-4.1-mini, q004). Cross-judge agreement is 76%, kappa 0.51. Templates change the majority outcome in 5/20 = 25% of cases. These are pairwise preferences; the pointwise score gaps were small and not significant.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Not applicable (judge methodology). It is relevant to BOAR's Haiku 1-5 judge, though the paper's setting is pairwise and uses OpenAI mini judges.

verdicts.claim: About 11 trials for majority vote to recover the 50-trial verdict with 95% probability; 15 for high-variance
verdicts.evidence: The abstract states 11 trials for 95% and 15 for high-variance questions. Table 6 disagrees: on hard questions, 15 trials give 90% fidelity and more than 50 are needed for 95%. The paper also recommends position randomisation and uncertainty reporting.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Not applicable. The repeat count must be re-measured for BOAR's pointwise 1-5 scores.
verdicts.corrected_claim: 11 trials recover the 50-trial pairwise reference verdict with 95% probability overall. For high-variance questions, Table 6 gives 15 trials for 90% fidelity and more than 50 for 95% (the abstract's '15 for 95%' conflicts with Table 6).

verdicts.claim: Judge error correctable with a small human calibration set via sensitivity/specificity plug-in correction; PPI-style biased under shift
verdicts.evidence: The method corrects BINARY judge verdicts using sensitivity/specificity, with CIs that cover both test and calibration uncertainty. Adaptive allocation uses a pilot of about 10 per label and Prop. 5.2. The intro states that existing methods can become biased under distribution shift (Sec. 8: the PPI-type difference estimator), while their estimator stays unbiased. Simulations use n=1000 and m=200; the Arena experiment uses a 90/10 split. Judges: GPT-4.1-mini, with Claude-Haiku-4.5 and others in the appendix. CC BY-SA 4.0, ICML 2026, v4 dated 2026-05-31. The bias statement was checked on the current version, not on v3 specifically.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Not applicable. BOAR's 1-5 scores must be binarised (e.g. correct = score >= 4) before this correction applies, and the calibration labels must come from humans.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The plug-in correction applies to binary judge verdicts (sensitivity/specificity), with CIs over test and calibration uncertainty and adaptive allocation of calibration labels. The paper shows existing estimators (including the PPI difference estimator) can be biased under test/calibration shift, while theirs is not. In simulations, m=200 calibration labels go with n=1000 test items.

verdicts.claim: LiteRT-LM Qwen3-1.7B wi4b32 on Galaxy S26: GPU ~40.6 tok/s decode vs CPU ~8.1; prefill ~550 vs ~60
verdicts.evidence: The card's numbers match exactly. It is a community measurement on a Galaxy S26 SM8850 with litert_lm_advanced_main v0.16.0, a 202-token prompt and 2 runs. The files require litert-lm 0.18.0 or newer. Apache-2.0. Caveats: the int8 file's CPU prefill is 238-245 (vs 48-76 for int4), which points to an unoptimised int4 CPU path, so the 5x/9x ratio is not a hardware property. GPU engine init takes 4.4-8.3 s. MMLU-100 is 64 for int4 vs 70 for BF16. llama.cpp CPU on the Pixel 8a already decodes 12-16 tok/s, faster than LiteRT CPU's 8 tok/s on a faster SoC.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Same model size and fully offline. Mali-G715 is untested, and the S26 Adreno numbers do not transfer.

verdicts.claim: Gemma 3 1B S24 Ultra: LiteRT-LM GPU prefill 2531 vs CPU 379, decode 49 vs 55; MediaPipe GPU 2585 per Google blog
verdicts.evidence: The card's LiteRT-LM table (int4 QAT, ctx 2048) gives CPU 379/55 and GPU 2531/49. MediaPipe GPU int4 QAT gives 2585/56 with TTFT 4.50 s; MediaPipe CPU int4 block128 at ctx 1280 gives 138/50. The Google Developers blog of 2025-03-12, 'Gemma 3 on mobile and web with Google AI Edge', quotes 2585 tok/s (S24 Ultra, performance governor). The licence is Gemma terms.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: A 1B model, offline. It is an Adreno GPU, not the Pixel 8a's Mali. It supports the view that the GPU helps prefill and TTFT, not decode.

verdicts.claim: Mobile LLM inference measurement study: NPU best at prefill, CPU best at decode; 10x NPU framework gaps; 39.7% energy saving
verdicts.evidence: Title: 'Is Your NPU Ready for LLMs?' (CC BY 4.0). The full HTML gives the details. Devices: Xiaomi 17 and OnePlus 15 (SM8850), Xiaomi 15 (SM8750), Xiaomi 14 (SM8650). Frameworks: llama.cpp, MNN, MLC-LLM, MLLM, GENIE. Models: Llama 3.2-1B/3B, Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, Phi-3.5-mini, all 4-bit. The 10x example is the OnePlus 15 with Qwen2.5-1.5B: GENIE NPU prefill 1463.7 vs llama.cpp 115.1 tok/s, with decode about 23 for both. llama.cpp CPU decode reaches 55.7 vs 23.0 for the NPU, and CPUs reach up to about 70 tok/s. The 39.7% saving comes from CPU frequency tuning during NPU inference; the NPU energy config saves 53.2%.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: It covers 1-3B models, offline. All devices are Qualcomm (no Tensor G3/Mali), so the direction transfers but the numbers do not.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On 4 Snapdragon phones (8 Gen 3 to 8 Elite Gen 5), 5 frameworks, and 1B-7.6B 4-bit models: NPUs win prefill (e.g. 1463.7 vs 115.1 tok/s for Qwen2.5-1.5B on a OnePlus 15), and CPU llama.cpp wins decode (55.7 vs 23.0 tok/s). NPU framework gaps exceed 10x. CPU frequency tuning saves up to 39.7% energy, and the NPU config saves 53.2%.

verdicts.claim: At 3-4B, single-pass answer NLL is weak (AUROC 0.63-0.69); SE (10 samples) 0.884 TriviaQA Llama-3.2-3B vs NLL 0.664.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Sequence-NLL AUROC across 3-4B models spans 0.504-0.690. TriviaQA/BioASQ/MedicalQA: Llama-3.2-3B 0.664/0.656/0.690, Qwen3-4B 0.632/0.663/0.613, Gemma-3-4B 0.504/0.647/0.635. SE with K=10, T=1 on TriviaQA: Llama 0.884, Qwen 0.844, Gemma 0.752. SE probe (Llama) 0.723. The same paper's single-pass prompt-hidden-state probe (PC probe, logistic regression, no sampling) reaches TriviaQA 0.813 (Llama 3B), 0.888 (Qwen3-4B, above SE) and 0.752 (Gemma). So the gap is NOT only reachable with samples, but it needs labels from the model's own answers. Test sets are about 150 questions.
verdicts.evidence: Main-results tables in the arXiv HTML. SE is defined with K=10 samples at T=1. PC probe = 'logistic regression classifier on prompt representations' at the last token before generation.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Partly. Raw NLL is a weak abstain signal; SE is too costly on the phone. A prompt-state probe is one forward pass and fits the budget if llama.cpp exposes hidden states, but it is untested below 3B and needs BOAR-labelled training data.

verdicts.claim: SAPLMA-style probes 0.80-0.83 cross-topic on Llama 2-7B fall to 0.56-0.59 on model-generated TriviaQA facts.
verdicts.evidence: Table 1 (Repr. avg): L16 0.8281, L20 0.8012, L24 0.7586, last 0.7326. Table 6 (TriviaQA-generated, threshold 0.5): 0.562 (last) to 0.594 (L16); threshold tuning does not help. Models are Llama 2-7B and OPT-6.7B only. Paper CC BY 4.0. Code repo exists; GitHub API shows no licence.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Indirectly. Measured at 7B only. The lesson (train probes on the model's own generations) transfers as a methodology rule, not as a number.

verdicts.claim: phi_first (first-token top-K normalized entropy, single greedy decode) mean AUROC 0.820 across three 7-8B models and two closed-book QA sets, vs semantic agreement 0.793 and surface self-consistency 0.791.
verdicts.evidence: Models: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Data: PopQA test and TriviaQA val, n=1000 each, K=100. phi_first per cell: PopQA 0.887/0.842/0.895, TriviaQA 0.794/0.727/0.772, mean 0.820. Sem. AU mean 0.793; AU-full mean 0.791. No NLL baseline is reported and there is no code link.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Fits the phone: it needs only top-n logits that llama.cpp already exposes, with no extra decode. Untested at <=3B and in RAG/multi-sentence answers, where the 'first content token' must be defined. Validate on the 1.7B dev traces before relying on it.

verdicts.claim: 0.5B-14B models on ARC-Challenge/TruthfulQA: Platt ECE as low as 0.02; certified autonomy at 20% risk for only 3 model-task pairs, none at 10%.
verdicts.evidence: Best Platt ECE is 0.015 (Qwen2.5-3B, ARC), rounded to 0.02 in the abstract. The 3 pairs certified at 20% risk are Qwen2.5-14B ARC (99.8% coverage), Qwen2.5-7B ARC (93.3%) and Qwen2.5-14B TruthfulQA (43.6%); none at 10%. 11 models: Qwen2.5-0.5/1.5/3/7/14B, Llama3.2-1B/3B, Llama3.1-8B, Gemma3-1B/4B/12B. Verbalized confidence, multiple-choice tasks, 25,168 predictions. No code; arXiv licence only.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Yes, as a negative result. No model <=4B was certified at any risk budget, so BOAR should report risk-coverage curves, not guarantees. The tasks are multiple choice, not open QA.

verdicts.claim: DeBERTa-v3-xsmall (MIT; 22M backbone + 48M embedding) SQuAD 2.0 dev 84.8 F1 / 82.0 EM; nbroad squad2 fine-tune (cc-by-4.0) 81.5/78.3 unofficial script, eval block F1 81.641 / EM 78.534; no on-device latency.
verdicts.evidence: The Microsoft card says 'License: mit', '22M backbone parameters', '48M parameters in the Embedding layer', and SQuAD 2.0 84.8/82.0. The nbroad card says cc-by-4.0 and 'I got 81.5/78.3 but I only did one run and I didn't use the official squad2 evaluation script'; its eval block gives squad_v2 EM 78.534 / F1 81.641. No latency is published.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Plausible as a ~70M-param gate/reader alongside the 1.7B within the RAM budget. Licences allow redistribution. Phone latency is unmeasured.

verdicts.claim: LLMQuoter: LoRA LLaMA-3.2-3B quoter (teacher Gemini Pro 1.5, HotpotQA 15k) lifts accuracy 1B 24.4->62.2, 3B 57.7->83.0, GPT-3.5 75.8->88.5; quoter F1 41.3->69.1; judge GPT-4.0.
verdicts.evidence: All numbers are exact. Quoter P 43.6->71.0, R 48.3->68.0. Data: 14.4k train/val + 600 test. LoRA has about 24M trainable params. Judge is 'OpenAI GPT-4.0' via DSPy. The full context is the long HotpotQA distractor set, unlike BOAR's short context. The code repo yurifacanha/LLMQuoter has licence null per the GitHub API, so the code is not redistributable as-is.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Promising, but the gain was measured against long 10-paragraph contexts. With BOAR's 2-5 short chunks the headroom is likely smaller. A quoter adds a second decode on the phone; a 1B quoter would be needed to fit the latency budget.

verdicts.claim: RoBERTa-large FT 90.2 vs Llama-3.2-3B FT 82.2 on SQuAD v2 grounding; ModernBERT-base 86.4 at 5.1e11 FLOPs vs Llama-3.2-1B 2.9e12 and 3B 7.0e12; yes/no task; no latency.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Numbers are exact: RoBERTa-base 75.8, RoBERTa-large 90.2 (1.1e12 FLOPs), ModernBERT-base 86.4 (5.1e11), Llama-3.2-1B FT 56.8 (2.9e12), Llama-3.2-3B FT 82.2 (7.0e12), Llama-3.1-8B FT 91.1, GPT-4o 0-shot 95.5. The task is binary relevance and no latency is reported. The code URL is github.com/chandar-lab/Hallucinate-less (not chandarlab), and the GitHub API returns Not Found, so code availability and licence are unknown. A fine-tuned 1B decoder does poorly (56.8).
verdicts.evidence: Table 1 of the arXiv HTML, mean ± std over 5 seeds. The GitHub API query for chandar-lab/Hallucinate-less returned 'Not Found'.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Supports an encoder gate (ModernBERT-base, about 149M) over asking a small decoder; it fits phone RAM. The gate must be trained by BOAR, since no public checkpoint was found.

verdicts.claim: Extractive readers beat generative on short-context QA and generalize better OOD; T5 encoder is a stronger extractive reader than RoBERTa (2022).
verdicts.evidence: The abstract states all three findings. The full text uses the MRQA benchmark (6 in-domain + 6 out-of-domain datasets) with readers RoBERTa, ELECTRA, T5-base and BART-large, fine-tuned; T5-large was excluded as 'too large (737M)'.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Weak transfer. It compares fine-tuned <=400M seq2seq generators with encoders, not an in-context 1.7B decoder LLM. Treat it only as motivation to re-test an encoder reader.

verdicts.claim: OCC-RAG-1.7B vs Qwen3-1.7B no-think: HotpotQA 47.7->60.9, MuSiQue 20.1->38.2, ConFiQA 64.8->81.4, MR 12.7->5.0, MuSiQue-Un 54.7->87.2; substring metrics; vendor-reported; citations as literal quotes; GGUF unverified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The table numbers are exact. Against Qwen3-1.7B think mode the gains shrink to: HotpotQA 60.9 vs 60.9 (0), MuSiQue 38.2 vs 30.7, ConFiQA 81.4 vs 70.4, MR 5.0 vs 8.3, MuSiQue-Un 87.2 vs 82.8. OCC cites by source id inside a 5-section structured trace (query analysis, source analysis, reasoning, status ANSWERABLE/UNANSWERABLE, answer), not literal quotes, so output length and latency must be measured. Training: about 3.25M pairs (43k abstain), roughly 9e9 tokens, distilled from a larger teacher. A GGUF exists: occ-ai/OCC-RAG-1.7B-GGUF, with Q4_K_M at 1.11 GB. Licence is MIT, confirmed on HF.
verdicts.evidence: Table 2 of arXiv 2606.00683 and the HF model card. The HF API lists occ-ai/OCC-RAG-1.7B-GGUF files Q4_0, Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K, Q8_0, F16 and BF16, with tag license:mit and base Qwen3-1.7B-Base. GitHub: optimal-cognitive-core/OCC-RAG.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Yes, as a same-size drop-in on the phone (Q4_K_M 1.11 GB, MIT). The open question is answer latency from its reasoning trace at 12-16 tok/s, plus fit with BOAR's prompt and citation format.

verdicts.claim: Pleias-RAG-1B (~1.2B) quotes literal passages; third-party: HotpotQA 48.5, MuSiQue 15.0, TAT-QA F1 8.4, ConFiQA MR 25.3, MuSiQue-Un 21.9; 3,126,691 examples at 4096 ctx; apache-2.0 + GGUF.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The licence (apache-2.0), the literal <ref> quote citations and the training figures (3,126,691 examples, about 9.47B tokens, 4096 ctx) are confirmed. The third-party numbers (48.5/15.0/8.4/ConFiQA In-Acc 37.3/MR 25.3/21.9) come from the OCC-RAG paper, a competing vendor's table; TAT-QA F1 8.4 points to a format mismatch, so treat them as a lower bound. The official GGUF is a single unquantized 2.39 GB file, so Q4 needs local quantization. The paper itself gives benchmarks only in figures and calls the model both 1B and 1.2B.
verdicts.evidence: arXiv 2504.18225 Section 3 (mid-training stats) and Section 4 (qualitative results only). HF card: apache-2.0. HF API: Pleias-RAG-1B-gguf contains only Pleias-RAG-1B.gguf, 2,393,458,272 bytes.
verdicts.applies_to_1_7b_offline: Usable on the phone after Q4 quantization, with a redistributable licence. Evidence of quality on general factual QA is weak, so treat it as a lower priority than OCC-RAG-1.7B.
